pages.text: In the evening, the inn grew quiet, and even Dad walked softly. "Shh—Soft Steps, Soft Whispers." But Kota pounded down the hall. A paper sliding door opened, and a sleepy guest peered out.
Dad put a finger to his lips. Kota pouted. "Quiet is boring!"
An elderly turtle came in slowly, yawning. "I'm so tired. I need a good sleep tonight." Kota's heels still bounced.
Dad whispered into Kota's ear. "When we're quiet, hidden sounds come out. Shall we find them?" Kota tilted their head. "Hidden sounds?"
Kota hushed their feet and stopped. Oh! Water babbled at the hall's end. "Found the water!" Kota called in a whisper.
"Anything else?" Crickets trilled from the yard. Dad smiled and whispered, "The quieter we are, the more sounds appear."
Kota tiptoed past the turtle's room. Soft sleeping breaths came from inside. Kota covered their mouth with both hands, tail shooting up.
Dad lifted Kota and turned silently around. Both kept mouths shut, cheeks puffed. Only the pink towel fluttered noiselessly.
Now, at night, Kota counted on fingers in whispers. "One, soft feet! Two, sliding doors gently! Three, whisper words!" Water babbled back from the hall's end.
Dad hugged Kota under the quilt. "Caring enough to be quiet is the prettiest sound." "Soft Steps, Soft Whispers..." Kota fell gently asleep.
